description:
Nous sommes une équipe passionnée par les sciences de la Terre, la data et le développement logiciel.

Notre projet : un outil web qui détecte les tendances du système terrestre à partir des données NASA (carte, séries temporelles, significativité statistique).

Nous recherchons : un(e) data scientist ou climatologue, un(e) designer et ou communicant(e) pour la démo. La maitrise de l'anglais est un plus. Motivé(e) ? Rejoignez-nous !
summary:
Earth Trend Detective is a web tool that helps people investigate how the Earth is changing. Users select a NASA dataset covering temperature, precipitation, evaporation, soil moisture, vegetation, air temperature or air quality, then choose a region and a study period within the dataset’s available dates. The tool displays a monthly time series, accounts for seasonal patterns, estimates a linear rate of change with a 95% confidence interval, and assesses statistical significance using a regression t-test and the Mann–Kendall test. It also reports Sen’s slope as a complementary rate estimate. Results are summarized in plain language, and users can compare two regions to see whether their estimated trends move in the same or opposite directions.

By bringing data from GISTEMP, MODIS, GPM IMERG, AIRS, OMI, MERRA-2 and GLDAS into one guided workflow, D2T helps users select Earth science variables, examine regional change over time and assess the statistical evidence for a trend. It gives students and the public an accessible way to explore NASA data, while making clear that statistical significance does not establish a cause.
details:
FEATURES AND HOW IT WORKS

Earth Trend Detective is an online tool that helps users explore changes in the Earth system using scientific data. Users select a variable and a region, either through the guided tour or directly on the map. The tool displays a monthly time series and estimates its trend. GISTEMP already provides temperature anomalies; for other variables, the seasonal cycle is removed prior to analysis.

The application estimates a rate of change displayed per decade, in the unit specific to the variable, along with its 95% confidence interval. It assesses statistical significance using a t-test on the linear slope and the Mann–Kendall test; the Sen slope provides a complementary estimate of the rate. Detailed results also include the Hamed–Rao test, which accounts for autocorrelation when available.

A plain-language summary indicates which variable is being studied, in which region, the direction of the trend, and whether the trend is statistically significant. A non-significant result is identified as such; the application notes that a longer time period could alter this result. The user can change the time period under study and compare two regions, even when their estimated trends are in opposite directions.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

NASA provides a wide variety of data on Earth, but it can be difficult to know which data to explore and how to interpret a trend. Earth Trend Detective aims to make this process more accessible to high school students, college students, teachers, and the general public. Each variable is accompanied by a simple definition, and the results and methods pages explain the calculations. Our goal is to help users examine the meaning and magnitude of a change, as well as the associated statistical evidence, without confusing statistical significance with causation. The tool could also serve as a teaching aid in the classroom.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

The variables currently available for analysis include GISTEMP, MODIS NDVI and EVI, GPM IMERG precipitation, MERRA-2 evaporation, GLDAS soil moisture, AIRS air temperature, and OMI nitrogen dioxide. Earthdata products are retrieved and downloaded using `earthaccess`; GISTEMP comes from the NASA GISS public download. NASA GIBS provides the geographic background of the map, not the values used in the calculations.

The backend uses Python and FastAPI; data is processed with xarray and stored in Zarr. The interface uses Vue 3, TypeScript, MapLibre GL JS, and Apache ECharts. Summaries are generated by deterministic rules, without a generative AI model.

Details on the methods and data are documented in the source description (docs/DATA_SOURCES.md), the summary generator (api/app/summary.py), and the catalog served by the API (api/app/main.py).
